title: StepRun
description: One row per (task, step, attempt). Source of truth is the per-job append-only logs/step-runs.jsonl, written through the Task Access append path (ADR-0024). The derived pipeline-history.db step_runs table is a rebuildable cross-task projection over every project's step-runs.jsonl (the ProjectChatIndex precedent; ADR-0023). ADR-0051.

id.description: Stable identifier: hash of (jobKey, stepId, attempt). Idempotent re-projection yields the same id.

jobKey.description: Canonical PROJ-NNN::jobId identity. Display names and filesystem paths are never persisted here.

pipelineDefVersion.description: Version of the pipeline definition (pipeline-definition.schema.json) this attempt executed against.

stepId.description: The step's slug within the definition.

stepLabel.description: Human-readable step name at run time (denormalised so history survives a later rename).

stepType.description: Body kind of the step that ran.

failureMode.description: Whether a failure of this step gated the pipeline.

orchestratorReaction.description: How the orchestrator treated this step's artifact.

runId.description: The task run/attempt this step belonged to (links to the run timeline, ADR-0049).

attempt.description: Which attempt of this step within the task (re-runs increment).

status.description: Terminal status of the step attempt.

finishedAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC finish time. Null while running (not yet appended).

exitCode.description: Script steps only. The command's exit code. Null for llm steps.

model.description: Llm steps only. The model actually used (may differ from the configured override after fallback).

costUsd.description: Llm steps only. Estimated dollar cost of the step.

artifactRef.description: Job-folder-relative path to the markdown artifact this step produced.

orchestratorVerdict.description: Review steps only. The orchestrator's decision after reading the artifact. Null for scripted steps.

reason.description: Short failure or skip reason; null on success.

summary.description: Short human-readable outcome for an on-demand attempt.
